known_facts_book1: Arrives at the head of a procession of ten soldiers carrying clubs, ten courtiers, the royal children, and the guests.
Her first words to Alice are 'Who is this?', addressed to the Knave, and her second are 'Off with her head!'
Orders the three gardeners beheaded for planting a white rose-tree, and Alice hides them in a flower-pot.
Screams 'Off with his head!' or 'Off with her head!' about once a minute at the croquet-ground.
Runs the croquet game with live flamingoes for mallets, hedgehogs for balls, and doubled-up soldiers for arches.
Sentences everyone but the King, herself and Alice to execution during the game.
Gave a great concert at which the Hatter sang, and sentenced him to death for murdering the time.
Sends Alice off with the Gryphon to hear the Mock Turtle's history.
At the trial, demands 'Sentence first — verdict afterwards.'
Turns purple and shouts 'Off with her head!' at Alice, who answers 'Who cares for you? You're nothing but a pack of cards!'

known_relations_book1.King: Rules the court beside him; he follows her about apologising and quietly pardoning the people she condemns.
known_relations_book1.Alice: Adversary from their first exchange; sentences her to death and is contradicted loudly and decidedly in return.
known_relations_book1.Knave: Puts him on trial for stealing her tarts; he carries the King's crown in her procession.
known_relations_book1.Duchess: Sentenced her to execution for boxing the royal ears; the Duchess's affection is plainly fear.
known_relations_book1.Gryphon: Orders him to take Alice to the Mock Turtle.
known_relations_book1.Hatter: Sentenced him to death at her concert; he trembles under her stare in the witness box.

not_in_this_book: anyone is actually beheaded in Wonderland
the Queen is the ruler of all Wonderland
the Queen of Hearts is Alice's aunt or relative
relationships: the Queen is married to the King (never stated; they are seated together on their throne as King and Queen of Hearts)

known_facts_book1: Walks beside the Queen in the procession; the Knave carries his crown on a crimson velvet cushion.
Says of the sleeping gardeners hidden by Alice, and of Alice herself, 'Consider, my dear: she is only a child!'
Pardons quietly behind the Queen's back everyone she has ordered executed.
Wears his crown over his judge's wig at the trial and serves as judge.
Tries to have Alice removed under 'Rule Forty-two: All persons more than a mile high to leave the court.'
Repeatedly tells the jury to consider their verdict, and reads the tart-stealing verse as evidence.
Interrogates the Hatter, the Duchess's cook and Alice as witnesses.

known_relations_book1.Queen: Rules beside her and spends the book softening her sentences.
known_relations_book1.Alice: Questions her at the trial and invents a rule to expel her; earlier reminds the Queen she is only a child.
known_relations_book1.Knave: Tries him for stealing the tarts.
known_relations_book1.Cheshire Cat: Objects to the Cat's manner of looking at him, and orders it beheaded — starting the argument about whether a head without a body can be cut off.

not_in_this_book: the King is afraid of the Queen to the point of hiding
the King has no role at the trial

known_facts_book1: Walks in the royal procession carrying the King's crown on a crimson velvet cushion.
Is tried for stealing the Queen's tarts, standing in chains before the court with a soldier on each side.
The accusation is read out as the nursery rhyme: 'The Queen of Hearts, she made some tarts... The Knave of Hearts, he stole those tarts, and took them quite away!'
Denies writing the verses produced as evidence — 'I didn't write it, and they can't prove I did: there's no name signed at the end' — and the King answers that not signing only makes it worse.
The trial breaks up before any verdict is reached, when Alice grows and the pack of cards flies at her.

known_relations_book1.Queen: Accused of stealing her tarts; she demands sentence before verdict.
known_relations_book1.Alice: No direct exchange; she is a witness at his trial and ends it by growing to full size.

sequel_only: the Knave appears in the Looking-Glass world

hallucination_signals: found guilty of stealing the tarts
